summary: T. R. Chintamani was an Indologist who earned his Ph.D. at the University of Madras under S. Kuppuswami Sastri. He served as Librarian at the Adyar Library and Research Centre (attested 1928) and Senior Lecturer at Madras in 1933.

Specializing in philosophy, Buddhist studies, and Indology, T. R. V. Murti earned a D.Litt. from Banaras Hindu University under Sarvepalli Radhakrishnan. He served at Oxford (~1949–1950), directed BHU's Centre for Advanced Study (~1953–1967), and taught at McMaster (~1970–1972).
T. S. Devadoss was a scholar of philosophy and Indology who held an affiliation with the University of Madras, attested in 1994, and served there as a professor (attested 2008).

T. S. Eliot studied at Harvard under George Santayana and Charles Rockwell Lanman, as well as at Paris and Merton College. A philosopher and scholar, he held posts at Birkbeck, University of London (~1916–1919) and the University of Chicago (~1950).

T. S. Rukmani is an Indology, philosophy, and religious studies scholar. She held posts at Miranda House (attested 1983–1989) and Concordia University as Chairperson of Hindu Studies in the Department of Religion (attested 1989).

T. S. Srinivasa Sastri was an Indology and philosophy scholar. He was affiliated with Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute (attested 1972 and 2007), serving there as a professor (attested 1984–1992).
T. Shrinivas Shastri is an Indologist who served at Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute as a Pandit (attested 1993) and Professor (attested 2026).

T. V. Ramachandra Dikshitar was an Indology and philosophy scholar. He served as Principal of Madras Sanskrit College (attested 1938) and Professor of Advaita Vedanta at Banaras Hindu University (attested 1946).

T. V. Vasudeva works in Indology and philosophy. He has been affiliated with the Kuppuswami Sastri Research Institute, serving on the Editorial Committee (attested 2001) and as Deputy Director (attested 2026).

T. V. Venkatachala Sastry is a linguist and Indologist who studied at the University of Mysore, where his supervisors included D. L. Narasimhachar and Harogadde Manappa Nayak. He taught at Osmania University (1959–1968) and Mysore (1968; Professor 1984–1994).
T. Venkatacharya was an Indologist who was affiliated with the Italian Institute for Africa and the East (attested 1971) and served as a professor at the University of Toronto (attested 1971–1979).

T. W. Rhys Davids was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and linguistics who earned a Ph.D. at Breslau under Adolf Friedrich Stenzler. He founded the Pali Text Society and held professorships at the University of London and Owens College/Manchester.
T. Y. Lee is a scholar in the field of Buddhist studies who completed studies at Mangala Vihara Buddhist Temple and the Buddhist and Pali College of Singapore.

Tadao Yoshikawa, a scholar of Sinology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies, was educated at Kyoto University. He taught as an associate professor at Kyoto University (1974; 1984–2000) and later served as a professor at Ryukoku University (2002).

Tadashi Inoue was a history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies scholar educated at the University of Tokyo. He held posts at Kyoto National Museum, Iida City Museum (Director 1988–2006), Nara University (1987), Bukkyo University (1995), and Kyoto University of the Arts (2000).
Tadashi Sekino was a scholar of history, archaeology, Sinology, and Buddhist studies who studied at the University of Tokyo (~1892–1895) and later served there as an emeritus professor (~1929–1935).

Tadashi Tani is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. He completed doctoral studies at Waseda University and studied under Yuichi Kajiyama at Kyoto University, serving as professor at National Institute of Technology, Kochi College (attested 1996–2000).
Tadashi Toda is a scholar in the field of Buddhist studies who completed his studies under Keiki Higashimoto and Kogen Mizuno.

Linguist Tadeusz Milewski earned his Ph.D. from the University of Lviv and completed his habilitation at Jagiellonian University, studying under Rozwadowski, Willman-Grabowska, Meillet, Vendryes, and Benveniste. He served as Professor of General Linguistics at Lublin and Jagiellonian.

Tadeusz Pobożniak was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Jagiellonian University under Jan Michał Rozwadowski and Helena Willman-Grabowska, earning an M.A. and Ph.D. He later served as a professor at Jagiellonian University (~1973–1975).
